main:
Two Working Parents? How to Never Miss a Dog Walk or Mix Up Whose Turn It Is

Use walk time reminders together with a shared family log, and you'll have fewer days with a missed walk, even when everyone is busy.

Common struggles for dual-income households

  • Mornings are a rush before work, so it's easy to forget the walk.
  • When you get home late, evening walk times end up all over the place.
  • Sometimes neither partner knows who walked the dog today.

Basic routine tips

  1. Set morning and evening walk times ahead of time
  2. Get in the habit of checking reminders right away
  3. Log the walk as soon as you're back so no one else doubles up

When it's unclear whose turn it is

Even with a set schedule, if there's no way to confirm a walk happened, things go wrong. Everyone thinks someone else went and nobody goes. Or the dog gets walked twice. And on days when plans suddenly change, a fixed schedule alone can't keep up.

  1. Log it right after the walk so there's a record that it's done
  2. Before heading out, check the log first
  3. Instead of a fixed schedule, look at the day's log and take turns as needed

POOPIEMATE routine reminders + family sharing

Pick your dog's walk times in POOPIEMATE (Morning, Late Morning, Afternoon, Evening), and it sends a reminder at each one. When one person goes and logs it, the rest of the family gets notified right away. No more asking "Who walked the dog today?" every time. On busy days, you can use Ask for help to ask another family member to take the walk.

Manage your walk routine with POOPIEMATE

FAQ

We both work and often miss walk times. How can we manage it?

Set walk times and get reminders, and you'll forget less often.

If family members walk the dog separately, can we avoid doubling up?

Yes. When one person logs a walk, the rest of the family gets notified right away, so nobody heads out for a walk that already happened.
